chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Khaythama, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Deliver to our Shias that whatever is with Allah cannot be attained except by deeds; and deliver to our Shias that the people with the utmost of regrets on the Day of Judgment would be the one who portrayed justice, then opposed it to something else'.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for those who appear just but act unjustly according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) emphasizes that divine reward is contingent upon authentic practice rather than mere reputation, highlighting the Shia concept of sincerity (ikhlas) in action. He specifically identifies the 'greatest regret' for those who project an image of justice (adl) while internally or practically deviating from it, a key theme in Shia theology regarding the integrity of the righteous. This warning underscores the danger of hypocrisy (nifaq) among the pious, where outward piety masks inner inconsistency.
